stories.headline: OpenAI measures how much coding agents speed up its own AI research
stories.summary: OpenAI has published its first measurement of how far coding agents accelerate its own research, finding the gains uneven: strong on some tasks, weak on others, hence the "jagged frontier". The source excerpt was unavailable, so the figures are unknown. The direction is toward task-by-task accounting of what agents can do inside a research pipeline, and away from a single headline number.
stories.take: OpenAI has now published measured agent speedups inside its own research, moving beyond benchmark scores as evidence.

stories.headline: Databricks maps four ways to let AI agents work inside regulated, auditable systems
stories.summary: Databricks' forward-deployed engineers sort agent work into four patterns: deterministic controls stay in charge, agents iterate against a deterministic judge, humans own judgement calls, and bounded autonomy runs inside a set envelope. In a reconciliation, the agent investigates the failure; it cannot become the control. Sort your use cases into these four before granting agents authority.
stories.take: Agent sign-off in regulated firms now depends on who holds authority at each step, not just model accuracy.

stories.headline: PIPETTE defenders reach near-zero attack success on static attacks and resist adaptive ones
stories.summary: Attack success rate in red-teaming does not predict how robust an agent becomes. Two leading reinforcement-learning attackers, RL-Hammer and PISmith, keep rediscovering the same tricks. PIPETTE, an arXiv preprint, rewards attack variety and trains defenders on-policy, reaching near-zero attack success on AgentDojo and ASB while keeping task performance close to the undefended baseline.
stories.take: Red-team scorecards now need attack diversity, where raw success rate once stood as the proxy for hardening.

stories.headline: Three AI readers from different providers fact-check text as well as the best single model
stories.summary: If this holds, fact-checking AI summaries may not need one strong model. GauntletScore, an arXiv preprint, asks three readers from different providers typed questions, logs each answer in an evidence ledger, and counts a contradiction only when two agree. It scores 79.51 balanced accuracy, level with the best published checker; per-claim predictions and the scoring script are public.
stories.take: Grounding checks for AI-written summaries now come with a per-claim evidence trail, where one model's verdict once stood alone.

stories.headline: A small model handles routine agent decisions and cuts cost by up to 91%
stories.summary: Early signal that agents needn't call a large model at every step. AnyS1, an arXiv preprint, mines decision points from over 1,000 public skill documents and trains a 4B pointer model to pick routine options, escalating when unsure. Episode cost falls 75-91% across three benchmarks; the SkillDP dataset is public.
stories.take: Routing routine agent steps to small models cuts episode cost 75-91% across three benchmarks, a preprint shows.

stories.headline: A new benchmark tests whether AI can judge engineering designs without running a simulation
stories.summary: If this holds, engineering judgement is a gap leaderboards miss. EJBench, an arXiv preprint, draws tasks from battery cold-plate simulations; answers come from converged simulations, not LLM judges. The best of ten frontier models, GPT-6 Astra, scores 0.71, with similar confidence on right and wrong answers. Splits, harness and leaderboard are public.
stories.take: Engineering sign-off tests now ask what a model concludes from past runs, where they once scored software operation.

stories.headline: Epic Games to remove Unreal Engine's visual scripting, citing AI agents, per IEEE Spectrum
stories.summary: Claude Code made an orphaned Unreal game, KinForge, playable without AWS servers in four hours of mostly hands-off work, per IEEE Spectrum. Epic's response: Unreal Engine 6 drops Blueprints for text-based Verse, and stores more assets as text. Early signal that engines are being redesigned for agents.
stories.take: Engine vendors now have to make project assets readable as text, or AI agents will skip their tools.
